blocked.name: linde van achterberg (Old Linden of Achterberg / 'Duizendjarige Linde')
blocked.reason: Private land. Dutch Wikipedia (nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oude_linde_van_Achterberg), a strong independent source with its own history section, states plainly the tree 'grows on private farmland' and is 'not openly accessible to the public' at the farm at Levendaalselaan 6, hamlet Laareind, municipality Rhenen. Hard rule 10 excludes private land regardless of fame; this one does not bend even though the tree is historically important. ADDITIONAL CONCERN, not the blocking reason but worth recording: the tree was severely damaged by storm Ciaran in autumn 2023 (central stem and crown broke out), was braced 26 April 2024, and its recovery is described as uncertain, so vitality would need a fresh check even if access changes. STORY MATERIAL FOR A FUTURE PASS, should access ever be confirmed: popularly called the 'duizendjarige linde' (thousand-year linden) but scientific estimates run 350-700 years, most experts favouring roughly 350 (consistent with bomenbieb's own 1650 planting band, ~376 years as of 2026); the hollow trunk has lost its oldest rings, which is why dating is uncertain. It was the site of the FIRST tree surgery ever performed in the Netherlands (1965-66, by brothers Jorn and Allrik Copijn, founders of the Copijn tree-care firm), using steel cables, iron rods and stem cleaning to save it after storm damage, a genuinely notable arboricultural-history fact. A 1922 legal covenant protecting the tree carried a 3,000-guilder penalty for violation. Ranked #4 in a 1989 Dutch linden top ten. Trunk circumference reported as roughly 6 metres (600 cm).
